name: Azur
title: Father of the false prophet Hananiah
summary: Azur is primarily known as the father of Hananiah, the false prophet from Gibeon who opposed the prophet Jeremiah. He is also mentioned in Nehemiah and Ezekiel as the name of other individuals. The name Azur means 'one who helps' and appears several times in the Old Testament associated with various people.

keyEvents.title: Father of the false prophet Hananiah
keyEvents.description: Azur is identified as the father of Hananiah from Gibeon, a prophet who falsely prophesied that the yoke of Babylon would be broken within two years.

keyEvents.title: Hananiah's false prophecy against Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: Azur's son Hananiah broke the symbolic yoke that Jeremiah was carrying and claimed that God would crush Babylon's power within two years—a prophecy that proved to be false.

keyEvents.title: God's judgment on Hananiah, Azur's son
keyEvents.description: Jeremiah prophesied that Hananiah, son of Azur, would die in the same year because he had preached rebellion against the Lord. Hananiah died two months later.

keyEvents.title: Azur mentioned in Ezekiel's vision
keyEvents.description: Another Azur is mentioned in Ezekiel as the father of Jaazaniah, one of the twenty-five men whom Ezekiel saw in a vision at the entrance to the Lord's house and who gave evil counsel in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Azur as a co-signer of the covenant
keyEvents.description: A person named Azur is mentioned among those who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah after returning from exile in Babylon.
